content:
This is a small park on the east side of Murry Hill, near the river that cuts Empire City in half.  The park has a few Red Maple, and a few Holly trees scattered throughout.  Various colors of climbing roses are growing up the trunks of the trees.  There are two, small, freshwater ponds in the park, that have water lilies floating on the surface, and salmon swimming beneath.  In the center of the park is a pavilion, with trellis densely packed with more climbing rose, and a mix of hawthorn and wormwood shrubs circling the trellis walls of the pavilion.  The floor of the pavilion is hewn stone.

On the west side of the park is a two story cottage that faces in towards the park, that looks to have been grown from various trees and bushes rather than built.  The windows are encased on the edges with wood and bark, the roof a thick canopy of limbs and leaves.  The only thing that looks fabricated is the large oaken door, set in a pointed horseshoe archway. (this Cottage cannot be entered)

In the middle of the park is a small granite Obelisk with the following words etched into its pristine surface:
"Within love and hope
the bond of family is found
that no darkness can divide"

A short, thin, male chinnokin is here.   His body is a mix of blues, silver, forest green, and black, but is covered densely with stylized images that seem to be a part of his skin.  His yellow and black eyes fixate on each person slowly taking them in.  The fins on his arms and legs slowly pull in to be nearly flush with his appendages.  He is wearing a sleeveless, black swallowtail blazer, unbuttoned, and a black skirt that goes below his knees.  On the left hip hangs a gleaming sickle, and on the right a short, thin length of metal.  Around his neck hangs two necklaces.  The one that stands out is that of a soft blue triangle pointing down with three wavy lines, edged with tiny red fruits.  The other necklace is a simple white, small wooden lute pick on a leather cord that goes through a hole in it.  When hes not in his cottage, he can be seen walking around here.
I approach the park, admiring the beauty of the topiary and cottage. I keep my distance from the chinnokin, though I will offer him a nervous wave if he catches me gawking.
He waves back with as good of a smile as he can muster
(lol sounds terrifying)
I edge a bit closer to him, now letting curiosity get the better of me. "Lo, there." I offer with a titter.
"Hello friend... How are you..... today?"

"Making my way, friend. I have never seen, a manner of being, such as you. How is it, we came. To meet in this, fine. Park?"
My manner of speaking is both rushed and filled with odd stops and starts, draped in an unfamiliar accent.
(we probably make quite a pair having a conversation, lol)

(I am going to have to go suddenly so we will have to meet up again soon"

"I am sorry.... but still adjusting to life.... would we speak again.... soon?"
There's a chill in the air that passes over Wintergreen
(also Devon, The Mender will send a message to anyone you need bright here today.  so @ them if they are friends that might help you)

(all good!)
"I do like this park, sir. We shall, see. Each other, again."
I pay the chill in the air no mind. *It's just the wind*, I tell myself.
*"Or ye could stay and bring a drink"* The faintest whisper sounds near inches from Wintergreen's right ear
I start. "Dolores?" I call, looking around for my pigeon friend.
Sounds of flapping wings from a much larger beast touchdown behind Wintergreen
A black owl hoots from atop a tree
I spin around, spooked. "I said . . . I liked your park!" I hollar out nervously. The words the wind whispered finally register. "A drink?" I look at the owl directly. "Do you . . . want a drink?"
*"Whisky..."* Wintergreen hears next to their left ear
I grin. "Well. That's my kind. Of g-g-g-ghost. Wait here." I head towards <#863311533328695367> to find whiskey.
I return with a bottle of whiskey in hand, cork off and a few shots already down the hatch. "Spirit? I've brought the whiskey! I hope you're . . . talkative. Because I have questions."
*"Ye pour ye ask"*
The chill spreads from your left to right side, as if pacing about you
"Uh . . ." hesitantly, I tip the whiskey bottle sideways, letting a few ounces spill to the ground.
An owl hoots in the distance
*"Ye ask"*
"What are you?"
*"Dead"*

(lol)
I laugh and take a pull for myself, then tip the bottle over again, giving the earth a more generous portion.
"Oh! Spirit, Tell. Me this. When will the clock tower, open?"
*"When the door is unlocked and the knob is pulled"*
*"Hell if I know I'm dead"*
I frown. "Hmm. Not that kind. Of spirit, eh? Well. Would you like. To tell me your story? Then, spirit?"
*"I've been a pirate, a sailor, a soldier, survived thirty seven shipwrecks and died once before this."* The voice says, as if laying out the lines of a riddle
*"I've been dead for... at least an hour now"* the voice fades away (to make a chicken pot pie) *"Visit with your spirits again Master Barkeep"*

"A spirit for a spirit." I take a bit more for myself, just enough to blur the edges a little, then pour about half the bottle onto the ground. "For your roots." I say to the plants below, then walk towards the pavilion.
It seems like a good place to play a few bars, so I pull out my horn again and test out the echos against the stone floor.
Using my magic to kick up eddies of wind, I make the leaves and loam of the park dance around the pavilion, playing along as they move.
(casting *gust*)

I bring my impromptu concert to an end and take one last stroll around the park. "Farewell, winds of Murray Park. I think I shall see you again very soon." I sketch a bow in the direction I saw the owl and depart, thinking I haven't explored the <#851195289850347540> yet.

(Hello!)
(jsut so you know, I will have to go to work in about an hour, so if we are still going, we will have to pause there) A voice calls to Mictlan encouraging him to come to the park and talk.
Mictlan drifts, not quite sure what they're hearing. It's... not what they expected, at least, and they settle with a ruffle of their feathers at the base of a tree.
"Hello friend... I am someone that has been sent here to mend.... and you seem to be a bit" he pauses to think of a polite way of putting it "pardon... there is no better way of saying it...... dead"
"I am. Dead. Yes," they say, language still a bit stilted from not being incredibly fluent with most things commonly spoken. "I was. Present."
"Would you like to be.... hmmm...." he shakes his head muttering something about webs and says quietly "not undead..... more like re-alive... " he perks up "Alive once again?"

"Yes. I would. Appreciate. Revival," Mictlan gives a slightly lopsided smile that halfway mirrors whatever they're talking to. Not quite as bright as usual. "I was. Wondering. Why I had not. Ascended."

the chinnokin grimaces "That is part of why I am here..... Something seems.... broken." he says looking at his hands then looks back up "there is a price to pay for being brought back...." he trails off
"What. Price," the smile drops off completely. The expression is difficult to parse, but their wings start fluttering slightly again in something like anxiety.
"Your faith." he says plainly "The people I bring back are tethered to my path.... should they deviate too far from it.... their body will wither once again"
"My. Faith?" They practically press themselves back into the tree. For someone who was *raised on* a very specific faith, not a good sentence. "Please. Elaborate. I. Do not. Understand."

"You may follow your god... but also must follow me.... there are 5 tenants a person must follow to stay in line with me" he pauses a second "like any path..... they can step off..... but walk too far.... and youll be lost once again."
"It's not. Like that," they consider, with a slight tilt of their head. "Which. Tenets."

"First... Life is precious.  You should always act to preserve life.  This does not mean you wont take life…. Only that to take a life, you must be saving more than is lost.  This is because we are all one…. We are all one…. people.  I dedicated my time in this realm before and the one beyond to saving lives, and healing souls.  I found my serenity making other people's lives better…. But I also understood that some beings cannot continue… if we wish to serve the greater good."  he pauses
"I. Already. Do that," they nod, searching in their ghost robes for a notebook to write everything down with. "Life is. Important. Lifespans. In particular. Are a tragedy. When shortened. Generally."

The Mender nods "So you already are one step on this path of mine.... Second is that Mercy is not weakness.  Showing mercy should not be seen as weakness.  It is easier to act out of anger and fear…. Than it is to control them and show compassion.  Do not look down upon those that show mercy…. And recognize when you should show mercy.  I rarely gave in to my anger, and the one time I did…. I didn't live to make amends.  A lifetime of patience and practiced mercy… lost in a moment of fear and weakness.  We all make mistakes, but we must learn from those mistakes, so learn from mine."
"Weakness," they echo with a puzzled sort of tilt to a few of their eyes. "That should be. Simple. Enough. It is an. Odd concept. But patience. And mercy. I theoretically. Understand. "

"Mercy isnt easy, but is worth seeking.... Third, No person should be a slave to another person.  I have seen many people broken by chains and whips… and no one should ever be in the bondage of another person's tyranny...  My people were in bondage and help never came.  The war that took my life was between other slavers... and people they were trying to enslave and kill.  I spent my life fighting for freedom... and gave my life fighting for freedom from my own fate."
"I was. Told. Many bedtime stories. About setting. Slavers. On fire," they inform the Mender eagerly. "I also. Dislike. Injustice."

With those words, The Mender smiles a fish faced smile "That is very good.... Fourth.... We are a part of nature and the natural order.  Be kind to the world around you.  Respect it… the trees…. Grass…. Moss…. Rivers…. We are all part of the ocean of life…. So do what you can to protect it.  All life…. From the smallest of small to biggest of big…. Is connected."
"Plants. Are alive. Someone. At a plant shop. Told me. Yesterday," Mictlan nods wisely. "I can. Do. Kindness. But. Isn't nature. Inherently. Unkind."
"When a salmon eats a tadpole.... the tadpole is not part of the salmon..... we are all connected in nature... so to harm it is to harm ourselves."

"You can cut down a tree to make a table..... thats not unkind.... but to cut down a tree jsut to cut it down..... to burn a forest to burn a forest...." with a bit of anger he says this next part "**To dissallow a body to take its place in earth**" he takes a moment to breathe "that is doing harm"

"But aren't. All sentient. Species. Part. Of nature." Mictlan would have furrowed their brows if they had them instead of feathers. "Some. Just create. Out of. More durable things. Also. Does that mean. I should start. Burying. Every dead body. I find."

"Thats my point... as i said mercy for other people... this is mercy for the rest.... that is kindness... and no... a body on the ground will become earth..... but a body reanimated.... forced into its own bondage to another's will.... that is the error.... People can come back..... but it takes a miracle to be brought back if you body was used in such a way....."
"Yesterday.... I saw my old body in such a manner.... and it almost prevented my return...."
"Oh. I see. So no. Animating. Dead bodies," they nod with a slight frown. "That is. Fair. I prefer. My interactions. Not be with. Rotting corpses."
The chinn has a little chuckle "I might have to remember those words.... you summed it up nicely"

"so the fifth and final tennant...." he pauses "Embrace the day…  I didn’t know my last day had come.  There are things I never got to say… to the school I had made.  No amount of penance can fix the things not done.  Don’t let regret live in yourself."
"Thank. You." Their posture becomes a bit more natural. "I think. I was. Given. That advice already. Live. Explore. Because my lifespan. Is. Pathetic. In. Grander schemes."
"So you agree to these tennants, and to follow my path?"
"Is. Your path. Different from. The tenets."
"Those are the path.... you follow those and you are on the path.... deviate too far" and he motions to you now
"youll be back to where you are"
"So basically. To get raised. I follow. Five rules. Most of the time. After. Or die."
"Should I. Be taking. Notes."

"yes... tho there is a..... umm whats the word.... process after you are back..... to align you.... for the next five days… when you wake… you must stay silent…. Find water to bathe in…. And spend one hour in quiet contemplation, meditating on your new found faith.  You are welcome to use the waters here, but know, you can not say a word…. From when you first sleep….. Until you have spent this hour.  If you fail this…. Your body will weaken and wither until you have fulfilled these tasks, or return to the grave.... after that.... only stepping off the path will wither you"

(This means you cannot speak during a long rest.  You can sign, write, etc, but cannot speak.  Further after a long rest, you must find water to be in while silent for one hour.  When you start the meditation and end you need to @ me so I can verify.  If you speak during these times, you will gain a level of exhaustion for the day that will not be removed by rest until you have completed this post long rest meditation.  After doing this 5 times, you are considered one of the faithful)

Mictlan really doesn't like labels, but they like being dead even less. It *sucks.* They nod, scratching the back of their head. Or, well, trying to and hitting a tree instead with their elbow. "Yes. I understand."
